notes: Comparing quadrupedal and hindlimb-only locomotion in the same intact cats before and after spinal transection separates state-dependent from condition-dependent changes in the hindlimb pattern: the spinal state produces convergence of stance and swing durations at high speed, improper ankle-hip coordination, and altered flexor burst timing, whereas the hindlimb-only condition itself shifts paw placement, yield magnitude, and some burst durations - so hindlimb-only intact locomotion, not quadrupedal, is the proper baseline for spinal-state comparisons.
animal_study: Perturb or deafferent the forelimbs during quadrupedal intact locomotion to test whether forelimb-derived signals produce the hindlimb-only-condition changes (paw placement, yield magnitude, burst timing); extend the intact-versus-spinal comparison across post-transection recovery time points.
robot_sim: When modeling spinal-state gait changes, validate against a hindlimb-only intact baseline rather than quadrupedal locomotion; implement intact versus spinal (supraspinal drive removed) controller variants and separate state-dependent effects (stance/swing convergence at speed, ankle-hip coordination) from condition-dependent ones.

notes: V2a (Chx10) interneurons fall into tonic, phasic, and delayed-onset classes with electrical coupling only within a class; about half fire rhythmically during NMDA/5-HT fictive locomotion, and the rhythmically active fraction increases at higher locomotor frequencies, providing a mechanism for the frequency-dependent shift in left-right coupling seen when these neurons are ablated.
animal_study: Optogenetically silence or genetically ablate V2a neurons (Chx10::DTA) across a locomotor speed series and quantify left-right phase changes to test the frequency-dependent recruitment mechanism; test serotonin's selective excitation of tonic-class V2a neurons in vivo.
robot_sim: Implement left-right coordination with a rhythmically active V2a commissural population whose recruitment grows with cycle frequency; ablating this population in the model should reproduce the frequency-dependent left-right coupling shift observed in Chx10::DTA mice.

notes: In the newborn rat, the locomotor rhythm network is restricted to the upper lumbar (L1/L2) segments: transmitter application there drives locomotor-like activity throughout the lumbar cord, whereas lower lumbar stimulation yields only tonic activity, and motoneurons receive their rhythmic synaptic drive directly from the L1/L2 network with no segmental relay - the mammalian CPG is localized, not segmentally distributed.
animal_study: Use partitioned-bath stimulation in other species and later developmental stages to test whether rostral (L1/L2) localization of rhythm generation is conserved; lesion L1/L2 to confirm loss of organized locomotor output.
robot_sim: Build a CPG model with the rhythm module localized rostrally and projecting to segmental motoneuron pools without local relays, and verify that direct caudal stimulation yields only tonic output while rostral activation drives alternation at all segments.

notes: Comprehensive synthesis of locomotor control across bipeds, tetrapods, and fish: spinal unit-burst-generator organization, interlimb coordination, load- and hip-position-dependent reflex regulation of the spinal CPG, tonic gating of reflexes from skin and group II/III afferents, and brainstem and cerebellar control - the canonical reference architecture for locomotor CPG models.
animal_study: Probe load-sensitivity and hip-position reflex regulation of the CPG in decerebrate animals across speeds, and record identified interneurons during locomotion to test the mosaic unit-burst-generator organization hypothesized in the chapter.
robot_sim: Use the chapter's architecture - unit burst generators per limb/joint, interlimb coordination pathways, and load and hip-position feedback gating the rhythm - as the skeleton for a locomotion controller, with the reviewed reflex gating (skin, group II/III) implemented as state-dependent pathway gains.
flags: Abstract is a section table of contents only; the feedback-related items (load sensitivity, hip position, group II/III gating) appear as topic headings without demonstrated pathways, so feedback was left empty rather than guessed.

notes: A model-predictive walking pattern generator computes a dynamically consistent center-of-mass trajectory and angular momentum for arbitrary contact configurations (uneven, sloppy, slippery terrain, closed grippers) fast enough for online use, integrated with an acyclic contact planner and second-order hierarchical inverse kinematics; demonstrated on HRP-2 for long-step walking and staircase climbing with handrail support.
robot_sim: Implement a fast MPC-based center-of-mass and angular-momentum pattern generator over arbitrary planned contact sequences as a biomechanical baseline layer for biped controllers, and compare its robustness on uneven or sparse contacts with CPG-reflex approaches.

notes: During fictive locomotion in semi-chronic spinal cats, low-threshold cutaneous nerve stimulation evokes predominantly short-latency (5-15 ms) excitatory reflexes in extensor and flexor motor nerves that are phase-modulated to peak during each nerve's active period, with occasional longer-latency responses modulated out of phase; the stereotypic modulation across muscles and animals implies the locomotor CPG exerts stereotypic control over cutaneous reflex interneurons.
animal_study: Map short-latency cutaneous reflex modulation systematically across the step cycle in trained chronic spinal cats to test whether the stereotypic extensor-dominant excitation persists with recovery; stimulate pairs of cutaneous nerves to test convergence onto shared reflex interneurons.
robot_sim: Add phase-gated cutaneous reflex pathways to motoneuron pools with gain peaking during each pool's own burst, plus an out-of-phase longer-latency component, and verify the stereotypic phase-dependent modulation the CPG exerts over cutaneous reflex transmission.
flags: Feedback mapping: short-latency excitation in extensors (triceps surae) maximal during their active period was mapped to Cutaneous stance modification, and excitation in the flexor semitendinosus to Cutaneous flexor excitation.

notes: Conference abstract: in an 8-joint salamander stepping model without feedback, trunk kinematics deviate from the EMG pattern, illustrating the effect of muscle dynamics (motion closer to a standing wave), and feedback in a 10-joint model modulates CPG activity.
robot_sim: Reproduce salamander stepping models with and without muscle dynamics and with CPG feedback modulation (8- versus 10-joint versions), quantifying how muscle dynamics decouple trunk kinematics from the EMG pattern and how feedback modulates the CPG.
flags: Abstract is two figure captions (conference abstract, about 50 words) - too thin to support afferent types, feedback vocabulary, or an animal_study field.

notes: An automatic parameter-setting method for synthetic nervous systems of non-spiking leaky integrator neurons on physical robots: motor-neuron activations required for stable walking are computed first from a model of the system, then network parameters are tuned so the circuit produces those activations under expected sensory feedback - successfully yielding adaptive rear-leg walking in an artificial-muscle dog robot and supporting the validity of current mammalian locomotion circuit models.
animal_study: Compare the motor-neuron activation patterns the method computes for dog hind legs with recorded dog hindlimb EMG during comparable walking to test whether the tuned network captures real activation structure; perturb expected sensory feedback and measure the adaptation response.
robot_sim: Apply the two-stage tuning recipe - solve for MN activations that produce stable walking, then fit SNS parameters so the circuit generates those activations under expected sensory feedback - and ablate individual sensory pathways to test their necessity for adaptive walking.
flags: Robotics study with no animal experiments; animals entries record the modeled biology only (dog hind legs, mammalian locomotion models).

notes: In the neonatal mouse, vestibular (VIIIth nerve) stimulation evokes slow polysynaptic excitatory responses in thoracic sympathetic preganglionic neurons with concomitant GABAergic inhibition, mediated predominantly indirectly through the ventrolateral medulla rather than by direct vestibulospinal projections, and these vestibulosympathetic connections are already functional at birth.
animal_study: Repeat the VIIIth-nerve stimulation assay in adult mice and in vestibular mutants to test whether the indirect ventrolateral-medulla pathway remains dominant with maturation; use genetic access to sympathetic preganglionic neurons for pathway-specific manipulation.
robot_sim: Model vestibular influence on autonomic and motor output as polysynaptic - relayed through a medullary node with mixed inhibition - rather than as direct vestibulospinal projections, and test response-latency and pharmacological signatures against ablation of the relay.
flags: Vestibular (VIIIth nerve) afferents and the vestibulosympathetic reflex have no entries in the afferent or Feedback vocabularies; both fields were left empty rather than forced.

notes: Trial-by-trial analysis of primate cerebellar neurons during voluntary head movements shows neuronal sensitivities dynamically tracking the comparison between predicted and actual sensory feedback: when the motor command-movement relationship is altered, neurons respond as if the movement were externally generated, and sensitivities decline with the time course of behavioral learning - direct evidence for a sensory-prediction-error computation with rapid internal-model updating.
animal_study: Record neuronal responses during externally imposed versus self-generated perturbations of voluntary movement before and after adaptation to test the sensory-prediction-error comparison directly; inactivate cerebellar regions to dissociate prediction from feedback responses.
robot_sim: Implement a cerebellar-style forward model that predicts the sensory consequences of motor commands, computes a trial-by-trial sensory prediction error, and updates its gains with a learning time course; ablating it should remove rapid re-adaptation to altered dynamics.
flags: Primate species not specified in the abstract; animals recorded as the closest vocabulary term Mammals.

notes: Review contrasting neurobiological and robotic approaches to walking control, emphasizing common control principles seen across species, reviewing robotic walking controller design with an emphasis on bipeds, identifying where robotic and neurobiological controllers parallel each other, and suggesting ways to bridge the gaps between the two fields.
animal_study: Test the common control principles extracted from biology - local leg-level reflex control layered on central drive - in reduced walking preparations where individual pathways can be manipulated.
robot_sim: Build hybrid controllers combining central pattern generators with the local, leg-level feedback loops highlighted as shared between animals and robots, and compare centralized versus decentralized architectures on the same walking platform.
flags: Abstract names no specific animal preparations (only common principles across species); animals left empty.

notes: Argues that muscle multifunctionality versus specialization determines the relative division of labor between neural and muscular control in vertebrates and invertebrates: the transformation from neural activation to muscle force depends on intrinsic neuromuscular properties, body structure, environmental forces, and behavioral context, so muscles are not single-function actuators and neural control complexity must be evaluated within that biomechanical context.
animal_study: Stimulate or block individual muscles in behaving animals across postures and loads to quantify context-dependent multifunctionality, testing the claim that muscle function cannot be inferred from anatomical arrangement alone.
robot_sim: Endow simulated muscles with realistic intrinsic and context-dependent properties, then measure how much neural control complexity is required as muscle multifunctionality varies - directly testing the chapter's neural-versus-muscular complexity trade-off.
flags: Chapter explicitly covers both vertebrates and invertebrates; the animals vocabulary has no general invertebrate entry, so only Vertebrates was recorded.

notes: An insect-inspired, mechanism-based gait controller with local rough-terrain reflexes drives an eight-legged demining robot in simulation over irregular terrain, obstacles on the order of half the tibia length, sparse terrain, and ditches - robust navigation achieved without complex sensing or terrain mapping, showing simple biologically inspired local rules scale to rough-terrain walking.
robot_sim: Implement mechanism-based gait control with insect-inspired local terrain reflexes (no terrain map, simple sensing) on multi-legged platforms, and ablate individual reflexes to quantify their contribution to obstacle and ditch traversal.

notes: A spiking neuromechanical salamander model with detailed adaptive-LIF locomotor circuits and a 3D body with realistic muscles replicates in vitro and in vivo swimming and trotting open-loop; intermediate-strength axial stretch (proprioceptive) feedback - conserved across ascending/descending and excitatory/inhibitory topologies - increases tail-beat frequency, reduces intersegmental phase lag, and expands the stable range of descending drives, whereas high feedback strength overrides central rhythms and degrades controllability: proprioception helps only while it does not dominate the CPG.
animal_study: In real salamanders, record axial EMG and kinematics across speeds to measure intersegmental phase lag and tail-beat frequency, and attenuate proprioceptive feedback pharmacologically to test whether coordination and frequency degrade as the model predicts.
robot_sim: Implement intermediate-strength axial stretch feedback in a spiking CPG coupled to a body model and sweep the feedback gain to reproduce the frequency increase, phase-lag reduction, and stability-region expansion at intermediate gains and the controllability loss at high gains; test topology-independence by swapping ascending/descending excitatory/inhibitory variants.
flags: Axial stretch (proprioceptive) feedback fits no Feedback vocabulary entry - feedback left empty per the guide; afferents mapped to Mechanosensory as the closest term. Consider adding a stretch-receptor feedback vocabulary entry.

notes: A biologically based neural controller built from cat hindlimb pathway data coordinates sagittal-plane trotting in a 14-joint planar rat model actuated by antagonistic Hill muscle pairs; changing the strength of a single inter-leg connection suffices to account for the phase-timing differences observed between individual trotting rats, identifying inter-leg coupling strength as a dominant determinant of interlimb coordination.
animal_study: Measure inter-leg phase relationships across individual rats (strains or gait variants) and test whether differences in spinal commissural pathway strength account for the phase-timing differences the model attributes to a single inter-leg connection.
robot_sim: Implement cat-derived hind-leg and inter-leg coordination networks on a 14-joint antagonist-Hill-muscle tetrapod model, vary the strength of the single inter-leg connection to reproduce inter-individual trot-timing differences, and ablate inter-leg connections to probe gait breakdown.

notes: In healthy humans, tonic stimulation - continuous muscle vibration, electrical stimulation of cutaneous nerves, or the postcontraction (Kohnstamm) state - elicits involuntary air-stepping in about half of subjects, with prominent hip and knee excursions but no ankle involvement unless small constant plantar loads (4-25 N) are applied; pattern characteristics and stability depend on the sensory input, and bilateral alternating movements are more stable than unidirectional ones with fewer spontaneous transitions.
animal_study: In spinalized or decerebrate animals, test whether tonic cutaneous or vibration input elicits air-stepping and whether small constant plantar loads recruit ankle movement, paralleling the human findings; compare unilateral versus bilateral pattern stability.
robot_sim: Implement tonic afferent input as a sufficient trigger for CPG rhythmogenesis in an air-stepping model, with load-dependent ankle recruitment from constant plantar forces and reduced transition frequency for bilateral alternating patterns.

notes: Extends concurrent design of walking controllers and parallel mechanical compliance (EHPC with fewer assumptions; CPC generalized beyond hybrid zero dynamics) with Lyapunov, boundedness, and input-to-state-stability robustness analysis, a step-by-step compass-gait design with MATLAB code, and hopper-robot experiments using pneumatic artificial muscles as tunable parallel compliance - a systematic route to co-designing actuator compliance and control for robust, efficient legged locomotion.
robot_sim: Co-design parallel compliance (e.g., pneumatic artificial muscles acting as tunable springs alongside the controller) with the walking controller using the EHPC/CPC procedure on a compass-gait model, and quantify robustness and energy gains versus controller-only designs.

notes: In the stick insect single middle-leg preparation, load signals from trochanteral campaniform sensilla couple thorax-coxa joint motoneuron activity to stepping of the distal leg segments: ablating the trochanteral sensilla abolishes the coupling, and stimulating them by rearward bending of the femur terminates protractor (swing) activity and initiates retractor (stance) activity - cuticular strain provides the interjoint timing signal linking proximal motoneuron timing to distal leg stepping.
feedback: trochanteral campaniform sensilla load signals to adjust MN magnitude
animal_study: Record trochanteral campaniform sensilla afferents during free walking under varying load to correlate strain signals with protractor/retractor switching; selectively ablate femoral versus trochanteral sensilla in intact walking animals to map their separate contributions.
robot_sim: Implement load-sensitive strain feedback that terminates swing (protractor) motoneuron activity and initiates stance (retractor) activity at load onset, coupling adjacent joints; ablating this pathway in the model should decouple proximal joint activity from distal leg stepping.
flags: The vocabulary entry names MN magnitude adjustment, but this paper demonstrates timing/switching of protractor-retractor motoneuron pools by trochanteral campaniform sensilla signals - consider a timing variant of that entry.

notes: Review proposing computational architectures for the mammalian locomotor CPG that integrate the genetically identified interneuron classes (V0D and V0V, V1, V2a, V2b, V3, Shox2) with ablation phenotypes, assigning them roles in rhythm generation, flexor-extensor interactions on each side of the cord, and commissural left-right coordination, and showing how such models can unify and predict mutant locomotor data.
animal_study: Genetically ablate or silence specific interneuron classes across speeds and gaits and compare the resulting coordination deficits with the review's architecture predictions; record identified cells during locomotion to test the proposed connectivity directly.
robot_sim: Implement the proposed two-level CPG with genetically identified interneuron classes assigned to rhythm generation, flexor-extensor interactions, and commissural left-right coordination, and reproduce mutant phenotypes by removing individual populations.

notes: A three-degree-of-freedom, energetically conservative horizontal-plane rigid-body model with compliant virtual legs in intermittent contact exhibits periodic gaits in which mechanics alone confers asymptotic stability of relative heading and body angular velocity, with gait and force characteristics matching insect running observations reasonably well - passive lateral dynamics can stabilize hexapod running without neural feedback.
animal_study: Perturb running insects with lateral impulses and measure heading and angular-velocity recovery against the model's passive-stability predictions; vary load or leg properties to test the parameter dependence of stability.
robot_sim: Implement the horizontal-plane compliant-virtual-leg model and verify that passive mechanics alone stabilizes heading and body angular velocity; use parameter sweeps (mass, moment of inertia, leg stiffness, length) to map stable gait regimes before adding any neural control.
flags: Passive-dynamic stability from leg mechanics was mapped to Biomechanically mediated preflexive feedback; the abstract does not use the term preflex itself.

notes: The Wilson-Cowan coupled nonlinear equations for localized excitatory and inhibitory neuron populations exhibit simple and multiple hysteresis, multiple stable states, and limit-cycle oscillations whose frequency is a monotonic function of stimulus intensity, with a formal result linking oscillation under one stimulus class to multistability under another - the foundational dynamical substrate for neural rhythm-generation models.
robot_sim: Use coupled excitatory/inhibitory population units as CPG building blocks, exploiting their monotonic frequency-versus-stimulus relation for drive-dependent cycle frequency and their hysteresis and multistability for gait-state switching and regime transitions.

notes: The turtle spinal cord contains separate CPGs for three forms of scratch, two forms of swim, and one flexion reflex, with multisecond motor memories, interneurons partially shared across behaviors (enabling motor pattern blends) alongside behavior-specific cells, and deletion analysis supporting unit burst generators organized per degree-of-freedom direction (hip-flexor, hip-extensor, knee-flexor, etc.) - an organizational complexity the classic flexor/extensor half-center scheme cannot capture.
animal_study: Apply simultaneous dual-behavior stimuli to test the blending mechanism predicted by partially shared interneurons; record single neurons across spontaneous deletions to further test unit-burst-generator organization.
robot_sim: Implement the CPG as unit burst generators per joint direction under a selection layer combining shared and behavior-specific interneurons, and reproduce motor pattern blends and deletions as signatures of that organization.

notes: In the actively stepping stick insect, femoral chordotonal organ signals from the femur-tibia joint pattern motoneuron activity of the adjacent coxa-trochanter joint: fCO elongation (signalling FT flexion) terminates depressor and initiates levator activity, relaxation does the reverse, largely independent of position or velocity parameters and of the intrajoint reflex reversal; fCO stimulation resets and entrains pilocarpine-induced fictive rhythmicity - proprioceptive input from one joint acts on the central rhythm-generating network of an adjacent joint.
animal_study: Record fCO afferent activity during intact walking and correlate joint-motion signals with the timing of levator/depressor transitions in the adjacent joint; test other leg pairs and joints for analogous interjoint proprioceptive patterning.
robot_sim: Wire a joint-angle proprioceptor (chordotonal-analog) into the rhythm-generating network of an adjacent joint so movement signals trigger and reset centrally generated antagonist transitions; verify reset and entrainment under rhythmic proprioceptor stimulation.

notes: A terrain-aware control strategy for dynamic legged locomotion that combines a convolutional-neural-network module evaluating candidate footholds from on-board perception with a model-predictive controller optimizing ground-reaction forces over the chosen contact sequence, demonstrated in HyQReal simulations traversing rough terrain under realistic on-board sensing and computation constraints.
robot_sim: Implement a CNN-based foothold scorer feeding a GRF-optimizing MPC contact sequence for rough-terrain legged locomotion under on-board compute limits, and benchmark against CPG/reflex controllers on the same terrain.

notes: Parabolic-flight experiments show the period of human voluntary rhythmic arm movements shortens systematically with increasing gravity, while in weightlessness it depends more on task instruction, matching a computational model of a CPG coupled to a simple pendulum in which the CPG exploits near-resonant driving - evidence that CPG mechanisms flexibly entrain rhythmic movement to changing gravitational and mechanical contexts.
animal_study: In animals, manipulate effective gravity or limb loading (added mass or buoyancy) and test whether rhythmic-movement frequency tracks the shifted mechanical resonance as the CPG-pendulum account predicts.
robot_sim: Couple an oscillator or CPG to a pendular limb plant under variable gravity and loading; verify frequency adaptation toward resonance and the loss of resonance-locking in weightlessness when the pattern is purely command-driven; ablate the coupling to test the mechanism.
